title: Sleepless on Wall Street: All-Night Stock Exchanges Coming Soon

title: US Job Growth Falls Short of Forecasts as Firms Remain Cautious
summary:
The US added fewer jobs than expected in September and wage growth slowed, signaling some caution among employers amid rising costs. 
Nonfarm payrolls increased 29,000 last month after a downward revision to the prior two months.
The unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, partly reflecting a growing workforce.
Rebecca Patterson, Senior Fellow at Council on Foreign Relations and Former Chief Investment Strategist at Bridgewater, reacts to US jobs. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Rise as Jobs Report Eases Fed-Hike Worries: Markets Wrap

title: French Bond Risk Hits Euro-Crisis Levels
summary:
French government bonds deepened this week’s slump, with investors demanding the biggest yield premium to hold the bonds over safer German debt since the region’s debt crisis.
Huw van Steenis, Partner at Apollo, discusses this as well as the overall European economic outlook. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Rebecca Patterson Warns On Fragile Bond Markets
summary:
Global markets are rallying on softer payrolls, but Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Rebecca Patterson warns that the real story is rising bond yields, ballooning deficits, and nervous investors. She explains why France leads her "fragile four," how hedge funds and AI-related debt are reshaping bond volatility and what this new era of higher rates means for portfolios and safe-haven assets.
Correct: Updated guest position (Source: Bloomberg)

title: NYC Private School That Inspired ‘Gossip Girl’ Cut by Moody’s

title: Snap-on CEO on Tariffs and China Risks

(Source: Bloomberg)

title: London's Bridge Troubles Spread with Waterloo at Risk of Closure
summary:
London's Waterloo Bridge faces closure within three years without urgent repairs, deepening concerns over the UK capital's crumbling river crossings. 

Are London's bridges really falling down? Harry Black explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: G7 to Release Up to 100 Million Barrels of Diesel, Crude

title: Credit Markets Sputter as Spreads Widen Most Since March
summary: Credit markets are showing signs of caution, as surging bond yields, growing inflation fears, and record borrowings make high-grade company debt seem like less of a bastion of safety.

title: Why Qatar Airlines Gets Cheaper Jet Fuel Outside of the Middle East
summary:
Why does an airline like Qatar Airways need to source jet fuel outside of its own oil-rich region?

David Kang, former group treasurer at Qatar Airways, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss why the company often gets a better deal on jet fuel by looking outside of its own national petroleum provider. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Factory Orders Edge Higher; G7 to Release Diesel, Crude
summary: US factory orders rose by 0.1% month-over-month in August. Michael McKee breaks down the numbers and also discusses the G7's plans to release as much as 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Odd Lots: How Airlines Actually Hedge Higher Fuel Prices
summary:
Fuel is a huge expense for airlines and with two major wars now affecting energy infrastructure, fuel prices across the board are higher and higher.

David Kang, former group treasurer at Qatar Airways, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss how airlines use swaps and options to hedge against future increases in the price of jet fuel. (Source: Bloomberg)
